68F, DIRECT OBSERVATION admission from PHYSICIAN REFERRAL.
OUTCOME: discharged alive
PRESENTING SYMPTOMS: Localized edema; Abdominal distension (gaseous); Diarrhea, unspecified; Unspecified urinary incontinence; Abnormal results of liver function studies
PRIMARY DIAGNOSIS: Encounter for antineoplastic chemotherapy
ACTIVE DIAGNOSES: Secondary malignant neoplasm of other specified sites; Malignant neoplasm of anus, unspecified; Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct; Secondary malignant neoplasm of unspecified lung; Secondary malignant neoplasm of brain; Syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone; Hypomagnesemia; Anemia in neoplastic disease; Anemia due to antineoplastic chemotherapy; Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis; Obstructive sleep apnea (adult) (pediatric)
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Encounter for antineoplastic chemotherapy; Encounter for desensitization to allergens; Personal history of nicotine dependence; Family history of malignant neoplasm of digestive organs
PROCEDURES: none
MEDICATIONS: 5% Dextrose 50mL IV; Ondansetron 16mg IV; EPINEPHrine (EpiPEN) 0.3mg IM; Albuterol Inhaler 1-2PUFF IH; Benzonatate 100mg PO; Dexamethasone Sod Phosphate 12mg IV; Irinotecan 2.3mg IV; Cetirizine 10mg PO; Famotidine 40mg PO; DiphenhydrAMINE 25mg IV; DICYCLOMine 10mg PO/NG; Sodium Chloride 0.9%  Flush 10mL IV; Guaifenesin-CODEINE Phosphate 15mL PO/NG; Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 5mL IV; Bag 1BAG IV; Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV; Heparin Flush (100 units/ml) 5mL IV; Atropine Sulfate 0.4mg IV; Lorazepam 1mg PO; LOPERamide 2-4mg PO/NG; Hydrocortisone Na Succ. 200mg IV; Acetaminophen 1000mg PO/NG
MICROBIOLOGY: none
SERVICES: OMED
WARDS: Hematology/Oncology Intermediate
_patient.note:
[1] The patient is a 68-year-old female admitted from direct observation.
[2] The patient presented with localized edema, abdominal distension, diarrhea, unspecified urinary incontinence, and abnormal results of liver function studies.
[3] The patient was admitted for encounter for antineoplastic chemotherapy.
[4] The patient has a history of secondary malignant neoplasm of other specified sites, malignant neoplasm of anus, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct, secondary malignant neoplasm of unspecified lung, secondary malignant neoplasm of brain, syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone, hypomagnesemia, anemia in neoplastic disease, anemia due to antineoplastic chemotherapy, gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis, and obstructive sleep apnea.
[5] The patient has a past medical history of encounter for antineoplastic chemotherapy, encounter for desensitization to allergens, personal history of nicotine dependence, and family history of malignant neoplasm of digestive organs.
[6] The patient has received 5% Dextrose 50mL IV, Ondansetron 16mg IV, EPINEPHrine (EpiPEN) 0.3mg IM, Albuterol Inhaler 1-2PUFF IH, Benzonatate 100mg PO, Dexamethasone Sod Phosphate 12mg IV, Irinotecan 2.3mg IV, Cetirizine 10mg PO, Famotidine 40mg PO, DiphenhydrAMINE 25mg IV, DICYCLOMine 10mg PO/NG, Sodium Chloride 0.9% Flush 10mL IV, Guaifenesin-CODEINE Phosphate 15mL PO/NG, Heparin Flush (10 units/ml) 5mL IV, Bag 1BAG IV, Magnesium Sulfate 4gm IV, Heparin Flush (100 units/ml) 5mL IV, Atropine Sulfate 0.4mg IV, Lorazepam 1mg PO, LOPERamide 2-4mg PO/NG, Hydrocortisone Na Succ. 200mg IV, and Acetaminophen 1000mg PO/NG.
[7] The patient was evaluated for syndrome of inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone and hypomagnesemia.
[8] The patient was treated with Ondansetron, EPINEPHrine, Albuterol, Benzonatate, Dexamethasone, Irinotecan, Cetirizine, Famotidine, DiphenhydrAMINE, DICYCLOMine, Sodium Chloride, Guaifenesin-CODEINE Phosphate, Heparin Flush, Bag, Magnesium Sulfate, Heparin Flush, Atropine Sulfate, Lorazepam, LOPERamide, Hydrocortisone Na Succ., and Acetaminophen.
[9] The patient was admitted to the Hematology/Oncology Intermediate ward.
[10] The patient was discharged alive.
